pr_title: [ML] Report thread settings per node for trained model deployments
pr_body:
When a trained model deployment is started the user may request specific
number of threads for inference and/or parallel forwarding. However,
when the pytorch process starts these settings are adjusted so that
the actual number of threads doesn't exceed the available number of
threads. This commit changes the result format so that other type of
results may be read from the process than just inference results.
We then introduce a result for reading the thread settings from the
process and we report it in the response of the trained model _stats API.

Closes #81149

issue_context.title: [ML] Allocation stats should report actual thread settings used
issue_context.body: PyTorch trained model deployments have 2 thread settings `inferenceThreads` and `modelThreads` which determine how compute resources are used. To prevent over-subscription the native process [imposes a limit on the settings](https://github.com/elastic/ml-cpp/blob/main/bin/pytorch_inference/Main.cc#L211) which are checked against `std::thread::hardware_concurrency()`. Any adjustments to the settings are logged but those log messages are not the most visible, it would be better to report back in the deployment stats that a setting was modified. This should be done per node as models are deployed across heterogenous nodes which can have different hardware profiles and values of `std::thread::hardware_concurrency()`.
comments: This issue is now about communicating to the java side the actual settings the process uses for reporting in the _stats API.

review_comments: Add a `continue` statement here. If there is an inference results there will not be a thread setting

It doesn't hurt to not have it like this though. I know we'll probably not be compounding results together, but we follow this pattern for autodetect and analytics. I'd rather we kept it like this here too.
